title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$
authors: Hongye Zhang, Boqin Song, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Ying Zhu, Tianping Ying, Mingquan He
abstract: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below $T_\mathrm{F}\sim70$ K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of $\sim30-80$ K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature $T_\mathrm{p}\sim20-25$ K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.
summary: This experimental work measures the thermoelectric response of the Kagome compound CsCr6Sb6, which exhibits flat bands due to hybridization. The measurements show that the Seebeck and Nernst signals are significantly enhanced by this hybridization, confirming the material's utility as a platform to study Kondo physics driven by flat bands.
main_problem: To investigate the hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response in the Kagome material CsCr6Sb6.
main_result: The study reveals a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response, establishing CsCr6Sb6 as a promising Kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics via transport measurements.
method: Charge and thermal transport measurements (resistivity, Seebeck coefficient, Nernst signal) were performed on single crystals using a Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS).
model_or_system: The system is CsCr6Sb6, a Kagome Kondo material where electronic states near the Fermi level are governed by the hybridization between flat bands and dispersive itinerant bands.
key_observables: Seebeck coefficient (Sxx), Nernst signal (Syx), longitudinal resistivity (rho_xx), and thermal conductivity (kappa).
important_parameters: Characteristic temperatures include the Kondo temperature (T_K = 15 K), the coherence temperature (T_F ~ 70 K), and the observed extrema temperature (T_p ~ 20-25 K).
main_assumptions: The analysis employs phenomenological models, such as decomposing resistivity into normal and Kondo contributions, and considering phonon drag contributions to the Seebeck effect.
figures_summary: Figures show the crystal structure, resistivity vs. temperature (with Kondo fitting), Hall resistivity vs. field/temperature, and measurements of the Seebeck and Nernst signals across various temperature ranges.
paper_structure: The paper presents experimental measurements of transport properties, analyzes the temperature dependence of the Seebeck and Nernst coefficients relative to characteristic energy scales (T_F, T_K), and discusses the implications of these findings for flat-band Kondo physics.
why_interesting: The strong correlation between hybridization, magnetic correlations, and transport properties in a geometrically frustrated lattice like the Kagome structure provides a rich playground for studying emergent quantum phenomena relevant to strongly correlated electron theory.
